answers.solution:
Done. Solution written to `~/solution-worker-dispatch-cwd-not-worktree.md`.

## What I found

**Root cause:** `cd <worktree> && hermes chat …` only sets the *launching shell's* cwd. The hermes agent's tool runtime resolves its cwd from the session/project profile (`-s coding-hermes-worker`), which points at the shared foreman checkout `~/gitreins`. So the first tool call runs in the main checkout, not the worktree. Aggravated by a shared session profile, `--ignore-rules`, and no preflight cwd check — both workers wrote the same file.

**Evidence:** `agent.log` shows caller cwd = worktree but tool cwd = main; worktrees clean; main dirty.

## Fix (two layers)
1. **Brief contract** — first line `MANDATORY WORKDIR: <abs>`, worker's first action `cd <abs> && pwd`, abort on mismatch; drop the misleading `cd` from the launcher.
2. **Dispatcher wrapper** — per-task `git worktree add`, injects the absolute workdir into the brief, `flock`s the shared checkout, and passes `--workdir` when the build supports it.

Plus the runbook recovery (stop workers → confirm one coherent diff → verify → commit from main → `wave=none:<reason>`) and a post-wave acceptance probe.

## Verified
Built a self-contained harness that emulates the buggy tool-runtime cwd, reproduces the failure, then applies the fix. **9/9 assertions pass, exit 0**:

```
PASS: buggy: main checkout is dirty
PASS: buggy: worktree A stayed clean
PASS: buggy: worktree B stayed clean
PASS: buggy: both sessions logged tool cwd = main
PASS: fixed: main checkout is clean
PASS: fixed: worktree A was modified
PASS: fixed: worktree B was modified
PASS: fixed: A canary points at A
PASS: fixed: B canary points at B
```

Run it yourself with `ROOT=/tmp/cwd-poc-fresh /tmp/repro-and-verify.sh` (full harness embedded in the doc, syntax-checked).

signatures.description:
Fleet wave dispatch: launching `hermes chat -q "$(cat brief)" -m --provider

-s coding-hermes-worker --ignore-rules -Q` with `cd &&` in front does NOT give the worker agent that worktree as its cwd. In the gitreins tick of 2026-10-20 two workers were dispatched with `cd ~/worktrees/gitreins-DF-GITREINS-POC-9x && hermes chat ...`; both agents resolved their terminal cwd to the shared foreman checkout (~/gitreins) and edited the SAME engine/quality_metrics.py concurrently, while both isolated worktrees stayed clean and unused. Diagnosis: inspect git status in the worktrees (clean) vs the main checkout (modified) and attribute the writes from ~/.hermes/logs/agent.log by session id; the agent's first tool call runs in the project workdir, not the shell's cwd. Recovery that worked: stop both workers, confirm the single coherent diff in the shared tree, verify it independently (tests + a foreman-written acceptance probe), then commit it from the main tree; treat the worktree isolation as not achieved and record wave=none:. Prevention: put the ABSOLUTE workdir in the brief and have the worker cd there itself (or use a per-task checkout), and never run two workers against one shared checkout when both may touch the same file.
